name: Facilo Prop 65 Hazard Notices for WooCommerce
author: facilo

sections.description:
Selling into California from WooCommerce? Put the Prop 65 warning on the right products in minutes, and get back to selling.

You choose the products or categories. The plugin writes the California Prop 65 warning from the wording in the regulation and shows it before the sale: on the product page, or behind a clearly marked WARNING link. It’s built for online sellers who need a Prop 65 website warning without paying a developer to add one.

This plugin is a display tool. It doesn’t tell you which products need a warning, it isn’t legal advice, and it can’t promise any legal result. Those decisions stay with you and your lawyer.

What you get

  • The right words, without the guesswork. Pick the hazard, name the chemical, and the proposition 65 warning is written for you, from 27 CCR 25603.
  • Food and dietary supplements covered. They get their own wording and web address, from 27 CCR 25607.2.
  • Only the products you choose. Set a warning on a category, and it reaches every product inside. Leave out the exceptions.
  • Both online methods. Show the full warning on the page, or a WARNING link that opens it.
  • The yellow warning symbol, done for you, in the place the rule describes.
  • Your label’s short form. If your label uses a short form, show the same words online.
  • Your supplier’s exact text. Sent warning materials? Paste them in and show them as they are.
  • A warning that isn’t skipped. Shop pages get a small WARNING link, because shoppers can add to cart without opening the product.
  • Works with your theme. Classic and block themes, with a block and a shortcode for page builders.
  • Light on your shop. It loads only on products with a warning, contacts no outside server, and stores nothing about your customers.

Prop 65 Warnings Pro

Pro is a separate paid plugin for shops that want a record and less manual work, at USD 59 a year for one site or USD 149 a year for up to five.

  • A record for every order, with the exact wording and date, ready to export if a notice arrives.
  • The full warning box only on California orders. Shoppers elsewhere see a small CA WARNING link.
  • Confirmation at checkout, on classic and block checkout.
  • Update your whole catalog from one CSV file, with a check before anything changes.
  • The official chemical list, built in.
  • Warnings per variation.
  • See which products still use the old short form ahead of 2028.

Prop 65 Warnings Pro gives you a record for every order, California-only warning boxes and bulk updates, as a separate plugin you add to this one.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin protect my shop from a Prop 65 claim?

No. It shows the warning you set up. No plugin can promise a legal result. Ask a lawyer about your own shop.

Do I need a Prop 65 warning?

We can’t answer that for you. The law doesn’t apply to a business with fewer than 10 employees (California Health and Safety Code 25249.11). Retailers are responsible only in certain cases, for example when they sell under their own brand, or when a supplier has sent them warning materials (27 CCR 25600.2). Partners and marketplaces can ask for a warning in any case.

Which chemical do I name?

Your manufacturer or supplier should tell you. The plugin doesn’t test or check your products.

Can I use the short warning from my label?

Online, you can use the short form if your product label uses it (27 CCR 25602). Otherwise use the full warning.

What changes in 2028?

The old short form with no chemical name is only for products made and labeled before January 1, 2028, whenever they’re sold. Newer short-form labels name the chemical. Nothing changes in your shop by itself.

Is a notice in my footer enough?

The rule says a warning isn’t prominent if the shopper must search the website for it. That’s why this plugin works on the product page.

Does it show the warning only to California customers?

The free plugin shows it to everyone. Pro can keep the full warning box to California orders.

What about food and supplements?

Choose “A food or dietary supplement” and the warning uses the food wording.

Does it work with the block checkout?

The free plugin doesn’t change your cart or checkout. Pro works with block and classic checkout.

What does it store?

Your warnings and which products they apply to. Nothing about your customers.
